tensorflow_desc: An end-to-end open-source platform for machine learning, providing comprehensive ecosystems of tools, libraries, and community resources to build and deploy ML-powered applications.
jax_desc: An open-source library designed for high-performance numerical computing and machine learning research, bringing hardware acceleration to native Python and NumPy code via automated differentiation and compilation wrappers.
flax_desc: A flexible and high-performance neural network library ecosystem built explicitly for JAX, designed to provide developers with clear, modifiable state and parameter management paths.
modularDesc:
Inference reimagined, from Kernel to Cloud.One unified stack.
Your model, any compute, one platform. Run AI across GPUs and CPUs - engineered for the most demanding inference workloads, from kernel to cloud.
servingDesc: Our high-performance, hardware-agnostic serving framework, MAX, automatically optimizes kernels and request execution across accelerators. 2x performance improvement over vLLM on diverse hardware through a single container and OpenAI-compatible API.
modelingDesc: Run 1000+ models like DeepSeek and Kimi out of the box with MAX. PyTorch-like model APIs and AI coding skills make it easy to port custom models in minutes.
gpuKernelsDesc: 100s of SOTA, composable kernels written in our high-performance systems language, Mojo. Extend or write custom GPU kernels for maximum performance across accelerators.
hardwareCompatibilityDesc: Modular was built to be natively heterogeneous. Run workloads seamlessly across NVIDIA, AMD, and Apple GPUs as well as Intel, AMD, and ARM CPUs.
mojoDesc:
Write like Python, run like C++.
Write fast code for diverse hardware, from CPUs to GPUs, without vendor lock-in, in a language that's both user friendly and memory safe.
maxDesc:
GenAI-native serving and modeling, built for performance.
Build once, deploy anywhere with a single programmable stack for high-performance GenAI on any hardware
selfHostedDesc:
Open infrastructure. Full control, made free.
Deploy MAX and Mojo on your infrastructure - one open-source container under 700MB that runs on NVIDIA, AMD, Apple & more. Write custom serving layers, models, kernels, profile workloads, and optimize every layer. Join our open source AI community today.
modular-infra_desc: A unified system execution tier engineered to handle complex model compilation and processing. It runs model evaluation workflows fluidly across heterogeneous processing nodes from a single local source codebase.
serving-engine_desc: A hardware-agnostic request serving framework built to optimize operation kernels and request execution queues locally. It serves diverse model types through a standardized self-hosted container using local API protocols.
modeling-layer_desc: Integrated model programming interfaces that allow custom software architectures to be ported, evaluated, and compiled into runnable local deployment formats within minutes.
gpu-kernels_desc: Low-level, composable compilation layers running directly on parallel hardware accelerators. This configuration allows developers to extend mathematical logic boundaries or build custom computing tasks to maximize performance.
hardware-compatibility_desc: A structural computing layer built to execute tasks seamlessly across various graphics architectures and processing systems, eliminating dependency on specific chipset vendors.
mojo_desc: A high-performance systems programming language that combines the accessibility of modern scripting syntax with the speed, memory safety, and layout control of native lower-level source compilation.
max_desc: A performance-focused serving and modeling subsystem designed to construct and deploy localized mathematical execution steps uniformly on diverse self-hosted setups.
self-hosted_desc: An isolated runtime configuration package built under 700MB for self-hosted data networks. It enables local profiling, custom layer composition, and full control over system hardware layers without external connections.
gpu_nvidia_driver_note: Software requirement: NVIDIA GPU driver 580 or later. Check your version with nvidia-smi. To update, see the NVIDIA driver docs. If your driver is older than 580, set the MODULAR_NVPTX_COMPILER_PATH environment variable to a system ptxas binary (for example, export MODULAR_NVPTX_COMPILER_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas).
gpu_amd_driver_note: Software requirement: AMD GPU driver 6.3.3 or later (MI355X requires ROCm 7.0 or later). For installation, see the Ubuntu native install guide.
code-generation_desc: Automated generation, review, and continuous refinement of software code through multi-step model evaluation cycles, utilizing optimized compilation techniques to maintain rapid execution loops.
image-generation_desc: Creation of high-quality visual assets and custom graphics from text descriptions, optimized to achieve maximum processing throughput across diverse infrastructure setups.
video-generation_desc: Production of synthesized motion video sequences directly from open-weight models on standard infrastructure, eliminating dependencies on proprietary external systems.
text-to-speech_desc: Conversion of written text into natural-sounding voice audio with minimal computational delay, ensuring unified execution across different host hardware setups.
agentic-ai-core_desc: Deploying foundational execution systems for autonomous software units capable of multi-step logical reasoning, structural planning, and programmatic tool utilization across local environments.
custom-models_desc: Developing and deploying bespoke, kernel-level model architectures across varying hardware environments using a single, unified codebase to eliminate vendor platform dependencies.
workflow-automation_desc: Chaining successive system calls to handle complex backend automation sequences—including document analysis, programmatic data routing, validation, and correction mechanisms.
ai-coding-agents_desc: Executing dense iterative programming loops for real-time application building, testing, and debugging via localized compiled processing protocols.
voice-to-action_desc: Consolidating speech recognition, semantic parsing, backend tool execution, and voice output generation into a unified data processing pipeline to eliminate transmission latencies.
on-device-agents_desc: Running self-contained logical models locally on edge consumer devices, allowing complex software processes to function completely offline without external server dependencies.
multi-agent-orchestration_desc: Coordinating networks of specialized models that communicate dynamically, utilizing structured system safety boundaries and central scheduling routines to complete unified objectives.
model-library_desc: Accessing and deploying a curated catalog of supported open-source frontier models locally in seconds, serving as the standardized evaluation hub for self-hosted execution environments.
hardware-selection-and-sourcing_what: The initial strategic phase for evaluating and purchasing physical computer components based on workload demands.
hardware-selection-and-sourcing_why: AI training requires intense computational resources. Choosing the right processors, accelerators, and fast memory upfront prevents project bottlenecks and avoids wasting capital on incompatible components.
hardware-setup_what: The process of assembling physical computing parts, arranging proper cooling systems, and connecting electrical power.
hardware-setup_why: Heavy computations generate high heat and draw significant amounts of electricity. Proper assembly prevents physical damage, overheating, and unstable system crashes during consecutive days of continuous load.
software-selection_what: The step for researching and selecting the programming languages, software engines, and library toolchains for the workflow.
software-selection_why: Different code tools interact with computer hardware differently. Selecting optimized systems ensures that mathematical operations translate directly into hardware actions without introducing execution lag.
software-setup_what: The process of installing operating systems, flashing drivers, matching configuration paths, and preparing software tools.
software-setup_why: Computers cannot automatically bridge abstract AI frameworks to raw electronic hardware. Proper setup establishes the foundational communication link between code libraries and execution processors.
llm-architecture-definition_what: The mathematical blueprint and code layout that defines the size, shape, data pathways, and internal layout of the network.
llm-architecture-definition_why: This dictates the raw intelligence capacity of the model. It maps how input data flows through layers and guides how parameters process information without overwhelming physical memory limits.
data-preparation_what: The processing pipeline for cleaning text data, removing duplicates, check for formatting errors, and structuring information for ingestion.
data-preparation_why: AI models are reflection engines that inherit the exact characteristics of the ingestion data. Clean data teaches the network logical patterns, while noisy data forces it to waste capacity memorizing clutter.
training-setup_what: Configuring the parameters of the learning loop, selecting error-tracking mathematics, and setting up memory-optimizing routines.
training-setup_why: Calculating mathematical changes across billions of points requires a massive amount of working memory. Proper configuration creates optimization guardrails to keep system memory stable.
pre-training_what: The primary learning phase where the model reads raw, generic text data at a massive scale to learn general grammar and foundational logic patterns.
pre-training_why: This is where a blank neural network develops its baseline understanding of language. Processing huge volumes of data allows the model to absorb syntax, definitions, and generic reasoning patterns.
launching-training-execution-run_what: Compiling the code, spinning up active data loading streams, and running the live processing loop across the hardware.
launching-training-execution-run_why: This is the active production step where the computer performs the actual learning computations. It requires smooth execution tracking and steady storage access to keep the hardware continuously saturated.
alignment-and-post-training_what: The process of fine-tuning a pre-trained model with targeted instruction scripts or safety guidelines to modify its output behavior.
alignment-and-post-training_why: A baseline pre-trained model only autocompletes text. Alignment shapes the model into a responsive, safe assistant capable of answering direct user queries.
evaluation-and-benchmarking_what: Testing the completed network against standardized question sets to track accuracy, logic speed, and performance.
evaluation-and-benchmarking_why: This determines if the training run was successful. It pinpoints where the network shows true understanding and highlights where it outputs mistakes or hallucinations.
compilation_what: The step where software tools translate abstract mathematical layers into highly efficient machine instructions built for a specific chip class.
compilation_why: Raw model code contains high abstraction overhead. Compiling condenses calculations into unified, efficient steps that unlock the full speed of the targeted hardware.
optimization_what: Applying speed enhancements, compression routines, or specialized token checking loops to accelerate responses.
optimization_why: This step maximizes performance efficiency, allowing the model to process inputs quickly and generate higher-quality outputs without requiring expensive hardware upgrades.
deployment_what: Packaging the compiled model file and transferring it into a production environment, such as a web server or a local application interface.
deployment_why: This moves the model out of an isolated development lab into an active state where it can serve end-users, accepting live questions and responding to outside requests.
inference_what: The live application mode where a deployed model processes an incoming user input prompt and generates a real-time text or code response.
inference_why: This is the final objective of the entire AI engineering lifecycle. Because the heavy training variables are dropped, inference uses minimal memory to deliver immediate answers.
